description: Generates millions of keyword-based password mutations in seconds.

summary.one_liner: psudohash is a Python command-line password wordlist generator that builds keyword-based mutations (leet substitutions, case changes, padding, years, numbering, word joins) for brute-force and hash-cracking work.
summary.what_it_does: The script takes a comma-separated list of keywords and produces a wordlist of human-style password variants. It applies leet-style character substitutions (editable mapping in the transformations list), case variations, and common padding strings read from common_padding_values.txt, either before or after each variant. It can append years with several separators (for example amazon2023, amazon_23) and append zero-padded numbered suffixes up to a limit. Keywords can be joined in original order (-i) or in all orderings (-c), with a custom separator, a maximum number of words per join, and minimum/maximum length filtering of the final output. Progress is shown with a progress bar, and results are written to a file (default output.txt).
use_cases: generate a password wordlist from company or personal keywords
build a custom dictionary for hash cracking
create mutated passwords for authorized penetration tests
test Wi-Fi, router or domain account passwords built from names and years
produce wordlists filtered by minimum or maximum password length
notable: Mimics human password patterns: leet substitutions, case changes, padding, and year suffixes
Leet mappings and year separators are editable in the source
In-order (-i) and all-order (-c) keyword joins with custom separators and max-combine size
Min/max length filtering of final words
Progress bar on each generation step
caveats: Output can grow to millions of entries, and the README notes duplicates may appear when options are combined
Length filters prevent the tool from pre-calculating the exact wordlist size
Customizing leet mappings and padding requires editing the source files
